rows.attack: Deliver a different secret
rows.defence: Dispute: the template decrypts and re-hashes; mismatch = Fraud

rows.attack: Commit to a block no client can decode, deliver it faithfully
rows.defence: Dispute also checks the block layout

rows.attack: Deliver noise
rows.defence: Nothing decrypts to the commitment

rows.attack: Repost another sale's R (or λ·R + k·G) so the buyer's dispute leaks that sale
rows.defence: deliver requires a proof of knowledge of r, bound to the sale; a dispute then only publishes r·B', which the seller already knew

rows.attack: List in a token they can recall or freeze, then drain or lock the escrow
rows.defence: XTM only

rows.attack: Never deliver, keep the buyer's funds locked
rows.defence: Delivery deadline; the buyer is owed everything, seller bond included

rows.attack: Squeeze the buyer's time to check and dispute
rows.defence: Windows of at least 3 epochs

rows.attack: Cash in before the buyer can dispute
rows.defence: claim_uncontested and payouts only after settlement

rows.attack: Malformed delivery (identity / non-canonical R, wrong length)
rows.defence: Refused

rows.attack: Cancel after being paid, or replay a cancellation
rows.defence: Listed-only, proof bound to the sale and the action

rows.attack: Bad terms (zero price or bond, windows out of range, invalid key)
rows.defence: Refused at list

rows.attack: A tiny seller bond against a high price, so delivering noise to an inattentive buyer pays off
rows.defence: The seller bond must be at least 10% of the price

rows.attack: A long delivery window and a short dispute window, so noise lands when the buyer is away
rows.defence: The dispute window must be at least the delivery window

rows.attack: A buyer bond above the price, turning any dispute into a trap for the buyer
rows.defence: The buyer bond must not exceed the price

rows.attack: Change the rules to lock the buyer out of dispute
rows.defence: No owner (OwnerRule::None)

rows.attack: List a clone of a real listing (same commitment and seller key) at a price of 1, then get the real seller to deliver to it
rows.defence: list requires a proof by the seller key over every term (msg_list): a clone must copy the exact price, bonds and windows, so it pays the real price

rows.attack: Claim fraud with a made-up S, a proof for another key, a bent or swapped proof, zero scalars
rows.defence: DLEQ verified on-chain against the registered sale key

rows.attack: Non-canonical scalars (malleability), degenerate points
rows.defence: Canonical scalars, canonical non-identity points

rows.attack: Replay a dispute proof from another sale
rows.defence: Challenge binds the component address

rows.attack: Read the secret, then dispute to be refunded
rows.defence: The honest delivery decrypts to the commitment: DisputeRejected, bond lost

rows.attack: Dispute after the window
rows.defence: Refused; the last epoch is still open

rows.attack: Underpay or overpay
rows.defence: Exactly price + bond

rows.attack: Pay in another token
rows.defence: XTM only

rows.attack: Register a key they do not hold, or the base key in place of the sale key
rows.defence: Proof by the registered key, bound to the sale

rows.attack: Buy a listing its seller stopped watching, then claim it undelivered to take the bond
rows.defence: Listings expire: buy is refused after the listing window; the seller can still cancel

rows.attack: Collect someone else's share, or the other side's
rows.defence: Payout signed by the payee's key, per action

rows.attack: Swap the outputs of a signed payout (mempool)
rows.defence: The signature covers the digest of the whole canonical transfer

rows.attack: Take more or less than owed
rows.defence: revealed_amount must equal what is owed

rows.attack: Reveal part of a payout to someone else
rows.defence: No revealed output; stealth outputs only

rows.attack: Mix outside coins or covenant claims into a payout
rows.defence: No stealth inputs, no covenant claims

rows.attack: Collect twice, or after losing
rows.defence: Owed amount zeroed before the transfer; nothing owed to the losing side

rows.attack: Get a payee to sign a transfer to someone else (a fake helper, a compromised wallet)
rows.defence: The CLI signs only transfers the template accepts for exactly --owed, and prints every output and its spend authorisation first; the payee must still check the outputs are theirs

rows.attack: Client and template disagree on the digest
rows.defence: Both decode and re-encode the transfer before hashing

rows.attack: Accept, cancel, deliver or take a payout for a party, from a hostile component in that party's own transaction
rows.defence: Actions need the party's Crypt key, not the signer

rows.attack: Accept with any key but the buyer's sale key, another action, another sale, another delivery
rows.defence: Proof bound to key, action, sale and R

rows.attack: Deliver without the seller key, or reuse a delivery signature on other content
rows.defence: Proof covers R and the ciphertext

rows.attack: Buy a listing twice
rows.defence: One sale per listing
